documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (USM AI Syllabus Policy; AI Usage Policy for Instruction)
documents.summary: The Provost page hosts the university AI vision, the syllabus policy requiring each course to state its AI rules with three template options, and promotional material on AI courses, grants, partnerships, workshops and the AI Taskforce.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Each instructor will determine the permitted use of artificial intelligence in each course' and gives three syllabus options (Encouraged Use, Permissible Use, Human-Generated Work Only), so the university sets no stance itself.

units.why: The vision states the aim that students develop 'critical thinking, curiosity, and ethical questioning' when engaging with AI; this is a principles statement, so P56 (institution-wide purpose and principles) rather than a skill-building rule.
units.anchor: develop and hone their capacity for critical thinking, curiosity, and ethical questioning
units.resolution_why: A coded actor admin, B coded all. The sentence is the university's own vision ('we are uniquely positioned to ensure our students develop and hone their capacity for critical thinking'), a statement of institutional purpose and not a rule that binds everyone, so admin. Type P56 and modality informs agree.

units.why: The vision says the university 'relies on the disciplinary expertise of our faculty to guide students' on appropriate use, so the university sets no rule and hands the decision to faculty; P04 fits because the decision sits with faculty.
units.anchor: relies on the disciplinary expertise of our faculty to guide students

units.why: The university commits to ensuring 'faculty, staff, and students have access to the training, resources, technology, and mentorship' needed; this is institutional provision of training and resources, so P70.
units.anchor: ensuring faculty, staff, and students have access to the training, resources, technology, and mentorship
units.fit_note: Also covers technology and mentorship, not only training.

units.why: The vision says students, faculty, staff, 'employers, and the broader community engage in meaningful discourse'; engaging community and employers on AI matches P88.
units.anchor: students, faculty, staff, employers, and the broader community engage in meaningful discourse
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. The vision says 'Our approach will foster an inclusive and collaborative environment where students, faculty, staff, employers, and the broader community engage in meaningful discourse', a stated commitment to engage the community and employers on AI. It is a real principle in the document, so it is kept as P88.

units.why: The elective offering says "Students will gain hands-on experience with Generative AI", a course that teaches AI use, so P44.
units.anchor: Students will gain hands-on experience with Generative AI and Orange Data Mining
units.frag_end: drag-and-drop platform that allows users to build, compare, and interpret
units.fit_note: A course description for AI literacy, not a training mandate.
units.resolution_why: A coded P70 with actor all and neutral; B coded P44 with actor student and encourage. The passage is a course description ('Students will gain hands-on experience with Generative AI'), that is, a course that teaches AI use, which matches P44 better than P70 (training offered or required of the community). It addresses students. It only describes what the course covers and does not urge AI use, so neutral. This is the only elective blurb either coder coded; it is kept because both found it.

units.why: The Responsible Use guidelines are described as establishing "a framework for the ethical, secure, and responsible use of AI at USM", an institution-wide framework, so P56.
units.anchor: establish a framework for the ethical, secure, and responsible use
units.frag_start: These guidelines establish a framework for
units.resolution_why: A coded actor admin, B coded all. The sentence describes the Responsible Use guidelines as setting 'a framework for the ethical, secure, and responsible use of AI at USM' for the whole community, so all. P56 and informs agree.

units.why: The syllabus policy says AI 'cannot be used for every type of educational endeavor' and can be misused, and asks to respect varied fields; it leaves fit to each field, so P04 (decision varies by field/instructor).
units.anchor: like any other tool, it cannot be used for every type of educational endeavor
units.fit_note: Rationale for why one rule cannot fit all fields; type captures only the resulting delegation.
units.resolution_why: A coded admin, B coded all. The passage is the university's rationale for leaving the decision to disciplines ('it cannot be used for every type of educational endeavor'), written by the institution and not addressed to a group of people, so admin. Both coders chose P04 and noted it is a rationale; both fit notes are kept.

units.why: Instructors 'are encouraged to guide discussions with students about ethical use within the discipline', which is explaining and discussing AI rules with students (P66); modality should. The passage encourages discussion, not AI use itself, so the unit stance is neutral.
units.anchor: Instructors are encouraged to guide discussions with students about ethical use
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on actor, phase, modality and type; A coded unit_stance encourage, B coded neutral. The source encourages instructors to hold discussions about ethical use. It does not encourage students to use AI, so neutral.

units.why: The page reports that 'reported academic integrity violations have increased significantly due to unauthorized use and misuse of artificial intelligence'; this is evidence on AI's effect on integrity, nearest P55.
units.anchor: reported academic integrity violations have increased significantly due to unauthorized use
units.fit_note: The evidence is about integrity violation counts, not learning or performance. Evidence is about rising integrity violations, not learning outcomes.

units.why: The text says 'Uncited or improperly attributed material used by artificial intelligence algorithms undermines academic integrity'; it warns that AI output carries unattributed sources, which is P120.
units.anchor: Uncited or improperly attributed material used by artificial intelligence algorithms undermines academic integrity

units.why: The policy 'requires courses to have a defined policy on whether using artificial intelligence is permissible and, if permitted, a statement on how it will be cited'; this is a mandate for a syllabus AI statement (P09), chosen over P24 because it binds the course and not the student.
units.anchor: requires courses to have a defined policy on whether using artificial intelligence is permissible
units.fit_note: Also requires a citation statement where AI is permitted.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on every code including unit_stance require. I changed unit_stance to neutral: the unit requires courses to state a policy, it does not require AI use. Both fit/why notes kept.

units.why: The policy 'requires courses to have a defined policy ... and, if permitted, a statement on how it will be cited'. This second requirement says what the course statement must contain, i.e. how AI use is cited. It binds the course (instructor) and not the student, so P09, must, before-course. P24 is the student's duty to disclose and does not fit.
units.anchor: if permitted, a statement on how it will be cited
units.frag_start: and, if permitted, a statement on
units.fit_note: Duty falls on the course to state a citation method, not directly on students to cite.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this clause; A folded it into the fit note of the unit for the first clause. They are two requirements in one sentence, so it is a separate unit here. B coded P24 and require; the duty falls on the course statement, so P09 (what the syllabus statement must say) and neutral. B's fit note is kept.

units.why: The text defines 'hallucinations' as 'inaccurate' outputs of language models; it warns outputs may be wrong, which matches P31's content though it is stated as fact and not as a duty to verify.
units.anchor: outputs that are inaccurate and based on perceived patterns
units.fit_note: States the problem only, with no instruction to verify.

units.why: The addendum is 'a preface to the existing usage level options (full usage, limited or outline usage, and no usage permitted)'. Naming the levels of use is P05; it defines the available levels and sets no action at a particular time, so the phase is general.
units.anchor: (full usage, limited or outline usage, and no usage permitted)
units.resolution_why: A coded phase before-course, B coded general. The passage only names the three usage levels (a definition of the options), so it belongs to general (definitions, principles, scope); type P05 and modality informs agree.

units.why: "By including this preface in individual courses, we intend to ensure the varied use and acceptance ... is communicated" asks courses to include the preface in syllabi, so P09, course-start.
units.anchor: By including this preface in individual courses, we intend to ensure the varied use
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this sentence ('By including this preface in individual courses, we intend to ensure the varied use and acceptance of artificial intelligence is communicated'); A coded the following sentence (faculty role) instead. It asks courses to include the preface in their syllabus, which is a separate rule from the faculty-role sentence, so it is kept as P09, course-start.

units.why: The text 'underscores the importance of each individual faculty member's role in examining the policy as it is made in each course'; the course-level instructor owns the rule, so P04.
units.anchor: each individual faculty member's role in examining the policy
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this sentence ('This underscores the importance of each individual faculty member's role in examining the policy as it is made in each course'); B coded the previous sentence (the preface in individual courses) instead, and the two sentences state different rules. A's unit is a real statement that the policy decision sits with each faculty member, so it is kept as P04 and B's unit is kept as its own unit.

units.why: The statement defines generative AI tools as 'capable of generating text, images, code or other types of content'; a definition setting what the policy covers is P61.
units.anchor: capable of generating text, images, code or other types of content
units.frag_start: Generative AI tools include types of

units.why: 'Each instructor will determine the permitted use of artificial intelligence in each course' puts the decision per instructor and course, so P04.
units.anchor: Each instructor will determine the permitted use of artificial intelligence in each course

units.why: 'Students are responsible for understanding what, if any, artificial intelligence tools are permitted' in each course; students must find and follow each course's rules, P78.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for understanding what, if any, artificial intelligence tools are permitted

units.why: Option 1 says AI tools 'are permitted in this class when usage complements the learning outcomes'; a default of permission is P02. P83 (align with learning outcomes) is also relevant but the main act is permission.
units.anchor: tools are permitted in this class when usage complements the learning outcomes
units.fit_note: Permission is conditioned on fit with learning outcomes (P83).
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance permit, B coded encourage. The sentence says tools 'are permitted in this class when usage complements the learning outcomes'. It allows use under a condition and does not urge it. The tier is titled 'Encouraged Use', but the unit_stance follows the sentence's own words, so permit. P02 and the fit note on P83 are shared.

units.why: It states AI 'can enhance your understanding and engagement with course material by providing differing perspectives and solutions', a benefit claim with no rule: P87.
units.anchor: enhance your understanding and engagement with course material by providing differing perspectives and solutions

units.why: Under Option 1 'You are required to cite usage of these tools in academic work', a duty to acknowledge AI use that conditions the permitted use: P24, must. The duty attaches to allowed use, so the unit stance is permit.
units.anchor: You are required to cite usage of these tools in academic work
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on every code (including unit_stance require). I changed unit_stance to permit: CODEBOOK reserves `require` for AI use that is itself required, and a citation duty is a condition on permitted use. Same change applied to the other disclosure and citation duties.

units.why: Under Option 1 students 'will be provided with examples of how to do so to ensure academic integrity'. The instructor commits to supply citation examples. No listed type covers an instructor giving citation examples (P25 is about what a citation holds), so UNCOVERED; the commitment is stated with 'will', so must.
units.anchor: will be provided with examples of how to do so to ensure academic integrity
units.frag_start: and will be provided with examples
units.uncovered_note: Students are given examples of how to cite AI use. Students are given worked examples of how to cite AI use.
units.resolution_why: A coded modality informs, B coded should. Both coded actor instructor, course-start and UNCOVERED. The sentence states a commitment ('will be provided with examples'), which binds the instructor, so must. The two uncovered notes say the same thing; A's is kept.

units.why: 'Citing AI usage promotes transparency and academic honesty' gives honesty and attribution as the reason for citing, which is P95 and not a skill-building reason.
units.anchor: Citing AI usage promotes transparency and academic honesty

units.why: Option 2 allows AI only in 'specific instances in this course' to assist learning, meaning AI is limited to listed assignments; P107 fits.
units.anchor: specific instances in this course where you will be allowed to use generative

units.why: It says limiting AI to specific assignments 'helps you develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills independently'; limits are justified by skill-building: P41.
units.anchor: helps you develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills independently

units.why: 'Specific assignments where AI use is acceptable will be noted by the instructor clearly and unambiguously' requires instructors to state AI expectations at assignment level: P09.
units.anchor: Specific assignments where AI use is acceptable will be noted by the instructor
units.resolution_why: A coded phase course-start, B coded during-work. The sentence ('Specific assignments where AI use is acceptable will be noted by the instructor clearly and unambiguously') is part of the syllabus text that communicates expectations, so course-start. Type P09 and modality must agree.

units.why: 'Any use of AI outside of acceptable use in the course is in violation of the Student Academic Integrity Policy'; unauthorized use is misconduct, P36. It also works as a fallback but the integrity classification is the main point.
units.anchor: Any use of AI outside of acceptable use in the course is in violation
units.frag_end: at The University of Southern Mississippi.
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance restrict, B coded prohibit. 'Any use of AI outside of acceptable use in the course is in violation' bans only the use outside what the instructor permits, so the stance is restrict (banned unless permitted), not prohibit. P36 and must-not agree.

units.why: The reason given is 'to develop your capacity for critical reasoning through the use of gained knowledge, experience, and perspective'; a skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: develop your capacity for critical reasoning through the use of gained knowledge
units.frag_start: The intention of this course is

units.why: Option 3 says 'the use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not permitted for classwork', a ban on AI for the course's work: P01.
units.anchor: the use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not permitted for classwork

units.why: 'Any use of AI tools for creation of content in this course may be considered a violation' of the integrity policy; AI misuse is classed as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: AI tools for creation of content in this course may be considered a violation
units.resolution_why: A coded modality informs, B coded must-not. The sentence says AI use 'may be considered a violation' of the integrity policy, which is hedged and warns of how the use may be judged. It does not itself ban, so informs. The ban is the previous sentence ('the use of generative AI ... is not permitted'), coded separately. P36 and prohibit agree.

units.why: Instructors 'should provide guidance regarding non-generative technologies, including translation and access software, spelling and grammar checkers'; routine features need separate guidance, so P100.
units.anchor: should provide guidance regarding non-generative technologies, including translation and access
units.fit_note: Says instructors should give guidance on these tools, not that they are exempt. Instructors are told to give guidance on such tools rather than exempting them outright.

units.why: Instructors 'may reserve the right to send any submitted work through AI detection software', which uses detection tools to find misuse: P40.
units.anchor: may reserve the right to send any submitted work through AI detection software
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance neutral, B coded permit. The rule lets instructors run detection software; it takes no position on whether students may use AI, so neutral. P40 and may agree.

units.why: "consequences deemed appropriate by the instructor" leaves penalties to the instructor, no concrete sanction; nearest P37, fit_note.
units.anchor: will result in consequences deemed appropriate by the instructor
units.frag_start: The use of unauthorized AI tools
units.fit_note: No concrete penalty is stated; the instructor chooses. Penalties are not stated in advance; the instructor decides them.
units.resolution_why: A coded modality must, B coded informs. 'The use of unauthorized AI tools will result in consequences deemed appropriate by the instructor' states that consequences follow but leaves them to the instructor, with no concrete penalty. It informs the student of that and sets no duty, so informs. Both coders added a fit note to P37; both are kept.

units.why: The page says courses offered through MAIN are 'available to University faculty, staff and students', giving AI training and education to the community: P70.
units.anchor: These courses are available to University faculty, staff and students.
units.frag_start: We are pleased to offer four

units.why: The university 'established the MAIN AI Lab' with workstations to support AI curricula, a capacity investment, P122.
units.anchor: established the MAIN AI Lab in Room 204 of Cook Library
units.frag_start: As a partner with MAIN, Southern
units.resolution_why: A coded actor admin and phase general, B coded instructor and before-course. The sentences describe the MAIN AI Lab that the university 'established' with the instruction that faculty can reserve it; the university is the actor who provides it, so admin, general. P122 and informs agree.

units.why: "$150 mini-grants to help members ... access an Al Pro tool" provides funded access to AI tools, so P51 (equitable access), informs; it is a grant rather than a no-cost rule, so fit_note.
units.anchor: $150 mini-grants to help members of the Southern
units.frag_start: The Library Al Access Program provides
units.fit_note: A grant for access, with no statement that paid tools are not required. Access support is a competitive grant, not a guarantee of free access.
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance encourage, B coded neutral. The Library program 'provides $150 mini-grants' for access to an AI Pro tool. It supports access but does not urge or require AI use, so neutral. Both coded P51 with fit notes; both are kept.

units.why: AI Integration Grants "support faculty in redesigning courses or academic programs to incorporate AI", institutional support for faculty adopting AI, so P63; fit is partial because it is funding rather than workshops.
units.anchor: support faculty in redesigning courses or academic programs to incorporate AI
units.fit_note: Funding to redesign courses around AI rather than workshops.
units.resolution_why: A coded P122, B coded P63. The Provost offers AI Integration Grants 'to support faculty in redesigning courses or academic programs to incorporate AI'. P122 covers institutional commitments and says it is 'not rules on AI use'; this is support aimed at faculty adopting AI in their teaching, which is where a reader looking for faculty support would look, so P63. B's fit note (funding rather than workshops) is kept.

units.why: The page lists "Generative AI Resources for Instructors" and other teaching links, directing instructors to further guidance, so P115.
units.anchor: Generative AI Resources for Instructors - MSU
units.frag_start: Generative AI Resources for Instructors - MSU
units.frag_end: Generative AI Resources for Instructors - MSU
units.resolution_why: Only B coded the 'Generative AI Resources for Instructors - MSU' link. It is one of the instructor-resource links under 'Teaching with AI', pointing instructors to outside guidance, so P115. A coded two other items of the same list; those are dropped as repeats of this same pointer (see notes).

units.why: The AI Taskforce 'consider the challenges and impacts of artificial intelligence' and its advice shapes resources; it names a body that advises on the AI policy and support, P80.
units.anchor: The AI Taskforce is composed of USM faculty who consider the challenges and impacts
units.fit_note: The Taskforce advises on resources; it is not named as policy owner.

units.why: The Office of the Provost 'lead workshops on best practices for the responsible use of AI' for students, faculty, staff and parents: training offered, P70.
units.anchor: lead workshops on best practices for the responsible use of AI
units.frag_start: As part of our efforts to
units.resolution_why: A coded actor admin, B coded all. The sentence is 'the Office of the Provost and other units lead workshops', so the office acts and nothing binds the whole community; admin. P70 and informs agree.

documents.unit: Office of the Provost / AI Taskforce
documents.title: USM Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence Guidelines
documents.summary: Campus-wide guidelines on ethical, secure and responsible AI use for education, research and administration, covering bias, oversight, privacy, accountability, acceptable and prohibited uses, training, enforcement and annual review.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines set principles but say 'The faculty will provide specific guidelines on permissible AI use in coursework' and 'faculty must approve its use for coursework', so course-level stance is left to faculty.

units.why: The introduction says the guidelines 'establish a framework for the ethical, secure, and responsible use of AI at USM' with stated values; an institution-wide framework: P56.
units.anchor: establish a framework for the ethical, secure, and responsible use of AI
units.frag_start: The University of Southern Mississippi (USM) recognizes
units.resolution_why: A coded actor admin, B coded all. The introduction describes guidelines that bind 'all students, faculty, staff, and affiliated individuals' (scope sentence), so all. P56 and informs agree.

units.why: The scope covers 'all students, faculty, staff, and affiliated individuals who develop, deploy, or utilize AI'; it defines who the policy binds: P61.
units.anchor: apply to all students, faculty, staff, and affiliated individuals
units.fit_note: Defines scope of persons and not what AI is.

units.why: 'AI output should be critically evaluated particularly in areas like admissions, grading, or hiring' because systems reflect bias; bias concern with an evaluate duty, P53 chosen over P31 since the stated reason is discrimination.
units.anchor: AI output should be critically evaluated particularly in areas like admissions, grading, or hiring
units.frag_start: Bias and Fairness: AI systems may
units.fit_note: Also tells users to evaluate output critically (P31).
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance restrict, B coded neutral (and anchored the preceding bias sentence). The text says AI output 'should be critically evaluated particularly in areas like admissions, grading, or hiring', a duty to evaluate output because of bias risk, which does not limit AI use itself, so neutral. Both coders chose P53 and should.

units.why: 'AI decisions with significant consequences must involve human oversight' and people must be able to 'override AI decisions'; humans stay responsible for decisions about people: P73.
units.anchor: AI decisions with significant consequences must involve human oversight

units.why: 'When AI systems interact directly with individuals ... informed consent is required' and the purpose, scope and impacts must be communicated. This is about telling people they deal with AI (P103) and getting consent. It conditions AI interaction on consent, so restrict; it binds whoever runs such systems, so all.
units.anchor: informed consent is required
units.frag_start: Informed Consent: When AI systems interact
units.frag_end: impacts of data collection and analysis.
units.fit_note: Requires consent and not only notice.
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all and unit_stance require; B coded admin and restrict. The consent rule binds anyone who runs AI that interacts with people, not an office, so all. Consent is a condition that limits such AI use, so restrict, not require. P103 and must agree; A's fit note kept.

units.why: 'Individuals should have the option to opt out without facing negative consequences' gives people an alternative to AI interaction. P51 covers 'alternatives exist'; P103 is about the right to know, which this does not state. It addresses everyone, should, and takes no side on AI use.
units.anchor: Individuals should have the option to opt out without facing negative consequences
units.fit_note: Opt-out right when AI interacts with people, not cost or access. Adds a right to opt out without penalty, not only a right to know.
units.resolution_why: A coded P51 (actor all, permit); B coded P103 (actor admin, neutral). The sentence gives a right to opt out. P103 is a right to know; P51 lists alternatives and accommodations, which is what an opt-out is, so P51. It binds anyone running AI that touches people, so all. It does not allow or limit AI, so neutral. Both fit notes are kept.

units.why: 'Students should disclose AI assistance where applicable' tells students to acknowledge AI use in their work: P24, with should as modality.
units.anchor: Students should disclose AI assistance where applicable
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance require, B coded permit. 'Students should disclose AI assistance where applicable' is a condition on permitted use, not a requirement to use AI, so permit (same reading as for the other disclosure duties). P24, should and student agree.

units.why: 'Faculty must approve its use for coursework, supervised research, and examinations', so AI use needs prior faculty approval: P107.
units.anchor: faculty must approve its use for coursework, supervised research, and examinations
units.resolution_why: A coded actor instructor and phase before-course, B coded student and during-work. The sentence is 'faculty must approve its use for coursework, supervised research, and examinations'; the duty to approve falls on faculty and approval comes before the work, so instructor, before-course. P107, must and restrict agree.

units.why: Users must 'avoid using high-risk data (e.g., student records, confidential research)' in AI unless verified secure by iTech; data protection with vetting: P50.
units.anchor: Avoid using high-risk data (e.g., student records, confidential research) unless verified secure by iTech
units.frag_start: Data Classification: Accurately classify all data

units.why: 'Personally identifiable information (PII) must be removed from datasets before AI analysis', personal data protection: P50.
units.anchor: Personally identifiable information (PII) must be removed from datasets before AI analysis
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance require, B coded restrict. PII 'must be removed from datasets before AI analysis' limits what data may go into AI, so restrict; nothing requires AI use. Type P50 and must agree.

units.why: 'AI use must adhere to applicable data privacy laws and regulations, including FERPA and HIPAA'; compliance with law, P77.
units.anchor: AI use must adhere to applicable data privacy laws and regulations, including FERPA and HIPAA
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance require, B coded neutral. 'AI use must adhere to applicable data privacy laws' invokes existing law and neither allows nor limits AI use beyond that, so neutral. P77 and must agree.

units.why: 'Limit data collection to what is strictly necessary' for AI applications; a privacy rule, P50.
units.anchor: Limit data collection to what is strictly necessary for AI
units.resolution_why: A coded phase general, modality must, restrict; B coded during-work, should, neutral. 'Limit data collection to what is strictly necessary' is a bare imperative in the Guiding Principles, so must and general. It limits data collected, not AI use, so neutral. P50 agrees.

units.why: Users must 'follow USM's information security protocols' for AI data; AI use falls under existing university policy: P77.
units.anchor: Follow USM's information security protocols to safeguard AI data
units.resolution_why: A coded phase general, must, require; B coded during-work, should, neutral. 'Follow USM's information security protocols' is a bare imperative in the principles on data, so must and general; it adds no limit on AI use itself, so neutral. P77 agrees.

units.why: Data shared externally for AI 'must comply with USM data policies, with explicit authorization'; a limit on sending university data to outside AI, closest to P65.
units.anchor: Any data shared externally for AI use must comply with USM data policies
units.fit_note: Applies to any data shared externally and is not limited to vendor contracts.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase general, B coded during-work. Sharing data externally is a principle stated under Data Privacy and Security, with no stage of work named, so general. P65, must and restrict agree.

units.why: "AI users and developers are accountable for verifying AI generated outputs" puts verification duty on users, so P31, must.
units.anchor: AI users and developers are accountable for verifying AI
units.frag_end: final decisions particularly in administrative functions and evaluations.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase general and unit_stance require; B coded during-work and neutral. 'AI users and developers are accountable for verifying AI generated outputs' is a duty exercised while using the output, so during-work, and it does not allow or limit AI use, so neutral. P31 and must agree.

units.why: Users must 'regularly assess AI systems for performance, security vulnerabilities, and ethical considerations'; monitoring of deployed AI: P98.
units.anchor: Regularly assess AI systems for performance, security vulnerabilities, and ethical considerations
units.resolution_why: A coded modality must and unit_stance require; B coded should and neutral. 'Regularly assess AI systems for performance, security vulnerabilities, and ethical considerations' is a bare imperative, so must, and a monitoring duty that takes no side on use, so neutral. P98 and over-time agree.

units.why: Users must 'promptly report any issues or malfunctions to the AI Incident Database (AIID), any required regulatory bodies, or the iTech Help Desk', a reporting duty: P71.
units.anchor: promptly report any issues or malfunctions to the AI Incident Database (AIID)
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance require, B coded neutral. The duty to 'promptly report any issues or malfunctions' is a reporting procedure, so neutral. P71 and must agree.

units.why: 'Inform users when AI is involved in decision making processes' is a duty to say when AI is in play: P103.
units.anchor: Inform users when AI is involved in decision making processes
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, must, require; B coded admin, should, neutral. 'Inform users when AI is involved in decision making processes' is a bare imperative, so must, and it binds whoever runs such decisions, so all. It is a notice duty that neither allows nor limits AI, so neutral. P103 agrees.

units.why: AI 'may be used' for 'generating content drafts, language translations, or creating study materials, provided outputs are reviewed by a human'; permitted low-risk uses, P14 for study materials, chosen as the closest type for a mixed list.
units.anchor: AI may be used for tasks such as generating content drafts, language translations
units.fit_note: List also covers drafts and translation. Also permits content drafts and translation, broader than study aids.

units.why: "provided outputs are reviewed by a human" conditions the low-risk uses on human review of output, so P31, must.
units.anchor: provided outputs are reviewed by a human
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this clause ('provided outputs are reviewed by a human'); A folded it into its unit for the sentence on low-risk uses. It is a separate condition (human review of outputs) on the permitted uses, so a separate unit: P31, must, restrict (permission depends on review).

units.why: "AI should not be used for tasks requiring accuracy and fairness" bars unsupervised AI in high-stakes evaluation, so P73 (decisions about people), should-not.
units.anchor: AI should not be used for tasks requiring accuracy and fairness
units.fit_note: Also covers hiring and any use of private information. Also covers grading, which P46/P101 treat separately.
units.resolution_why: A coded P101 (conditions on AI-assisted grading), B coded P73. The sentence says AI 'should not be used for tasks requiring accuracy and fairness, such as evaluations in hiring, grading, or any context involving private information without thorough human oversight and verification'. Grading is one example among hiring and private-information contexts, so P101 is too narrow; the rule keeps humans responsible for evaluations of people, so P73. Both fit notes are kept.

units.why: "final accountability rests with staff" assigns responsibility for administrative AI use to staff, so P76 (administrative AI), informs.
units.anchor: AI can enhance administrative processes, but final accountability rests with staff
units.frag_end: significantly affect individuals without human review.
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance permit, B coded neutral. 'AI can enhance administrative processes, but final accountability rests with staff' assigns accountability and does not set a permission, so neutral. P76, ta-staff and informs agree.

units.why: 'AI must not independently make decisions that significantly affect individuals without human review'; no sole AI decisions about people: P73.

notes: Reconciled from coder A and coder B. Three university-level documents; no school, computing or course documents were found at collection time. Document 1 is a long web page: promotional content (events, resource lists, taskforce roster, contacts, elective course blurbs other than one) was not coded. Dropped single-coder units on doc 1: A's 'prepared to succeed in their chosen disciplines and professional ambitions' (clause of a sentence already coded), A's 'USM began its partnership with MAIN in fall 2024.' (news item), A's 'Rethinking Course Assignments and Assessments' and 'How to Write ChatGPT Prompts to Get the Best Results' (titles in a resource link list; one pointer unit, B's, is kept). Doc 2: A's uncovered note for the accreditation sentence was 'Generative AI in accreditation work should be used by people who understand it and follow SACSCOC's guidelines'; resolved into P76, so no uncovered unit remains. Documents 1 and 3 repeat the three-tier syllabus text and were coded separately. Unit stance values for disclosure and citation duties follow CODEBOOK (permit), not require.
